root_cause.text: In `mm/slub.c`’s `__do_krealloc()`/`kvrealloc_node_align_noprof()` fallback realloc paths, the old object size was computed too late and then reused unbounded for `memcpy()`, so forced NUMA-node/alignment reallocation could copy 0 bytes or overflow the smaller new allocation when shrinking.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves the `is_kfence_address()`/`ksize` size calculation before the `goto alloc_new` NUMA check, and changes `memcpy(ret, ..., orig_size ?: ks)` to `memcpy(..., min(new_size, (size_t)(orig_size ?: ks)))`; it also changes `kvrealloc_node_align_noprof()` from `memcpy(..., ksize(p))` to `memcpy(..., min(size, ksize(p)))`, matching the CVE description that the fallback path had “copy 0 bytes” data loss and an out-of-bounds write when shrinking.

intent_record.intent_summary: __do_krealloc() no longer performs a special alloc_new fallback for __GFP_THISNODE mismatched-node reallocations.
intent_record.what: The diff removes a block of comments and a conditional branch from __do_krealloc() that previously checked for __GFP_THISNODE with a different NUMA node and, in that case, jumped to alloc_new.
intent_record.how: After this change, __do_krealloc() no longer forces a fresh allocation solely because __GFP_THISNODE was set and the requested node differed from the original allocation's node; that special-case path is eliminated, so the function proceeds into the normal realloc logic instead of immediately attempting alloc_new for that condition.

intent_record.intent_summary: __do_krealloc now honors __GFP_THISNODE by forcing a new allocation on the requested NUMA node even when resizing is otherwise unnecessary.
intent_record.what: A new comment and conditional branch were added in __do_krealloc(). The code now checks whether __GFP_THISNODE is set, the target NUMA node is valid, and it differs from the node of the existing allocation; if so, it jumps to alloc_new before the existing size-fit check.
intent_record.how: This changes realloc behavior so that when a caller explicitly requests a specific NUMA node via __GFP_THISNODE, an allocation will be moved to that node even if the current buffer is already large enough. Without this case, the old allocation would have been preserved when no size growth was needed.

intent_record.intent_summary: Limit krealloc data copying to the valid new allocation size to avoid incorrect memory access.
intent_record.what: The memcpy length in __do_krealloc() was changed from copying the full original allocation size expression `orig_size ?: ks` to copying only `min(new_size, (size_t)(orig_size ?: ks))`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, reallocation now copies no more than the smaller of the requested new size and the original size, preventing memcpy from reading or writing beyond the destination size when shrinking or when size calculations differ.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix kvrealloc to copy only the valid overlapping portion of the old allocation when resizing.
intent_record.what: In kvrealloc_node_align_noprof(), the memcpy() source length argument was changed from ksize(p) to min(size, ksize(p)) while copying from the old allocation into the new buffer.
intent_record.how: This limits the amount of data copied during reallocation to the smaller of the requested new size and the old allocation size, preventing reads and copies beyond the destination's intended size when shrinking an allocation and preserving correct copy bounds.

relevance_review.reason: The change only adjusts __do_krealloc behavior to force NUMA-node allocation for __GFP_THISNODE, but it does not address the buggy size computation or unsafe memcpy handling in the fallback realloc paths that caused the vulnerability.

The changes directly match the root cause: they fix kvrealloc/krealloc fallback resizing so copying is limited to the valid overlapping size, preventing incorrect memcpy behavior when reallocating to a smaller or differently aligned allocation.

The change affects __do_krealloc()’s fallback realloc behavior for __GFP_THISNODE mismatched-node cases, which is directly in the code path implicated by the root cause involving unsafe fallback reallocation and memcpy size handling.

candidates.rationale: This forced fallback into the alloc_new path for __GFP_THISNODE mismatched-node reallocations is the trigger for the problematic resize path described in the root cause, where the old size handling later becomes unsafe during memcpy.

This memcpy used the old object size directly as the copy length, which is the vulnerable behavior: in the fallback realloc path the size could be computed too late and then reused unbounded, leading to copying zero bytes or overrunning the smaller new allocation when shrinking.
This copy uses ksize(p) for the entire transfer, which can exceed the size of the newly allocated destination during kvrealloc fallback resizing, matching the overflow described in the root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the direct vulnerable copy in __do_krealloc(): it uses the old object size as the memcpy length in the fallback realloc path, which can be computed too late and then reused unbounded, causing zero-length copies or overflow when the new allocation is smaller.

This kvrealloc fallback copy transfers ksize(p) bytes without bounding the copy to the newly allocated destination size, matching the root cause where forced reallocation can overrun the smaller new allocation during shrinking.
